text:
Priya Sharma: Noticed recurring p99 blips when coalesced batches are formed at the same time as big kv-cache evictions. Wondering if we should move away from strict lease-slot counts toward a "soft token" layer that can be reclaimed under cache pressure. Thoughts? :mag:

Chen Li: Soft tokens sounds promising. How do you envision reclamation happening? Immediate revoke will re-introduce latency spikes.

Ravi Menon: Agreed — revocation should be cooperative: grant a soft token but mark the batch as preemptible. Runtime can give a gentle eviction hint and prefer dropping older preemptible coalesced batches when under memory pressure.

Avery Patel: Important: keep a tiny deterministic fast-path for single-shot tiny requests. Those should never be preempted by coalesced batches.

Marta Gomez: Observability ask: we need a time-aligned view of (coalesced_batch_size, kv_eviction_rate, p99_latency, preemptible_drops) before we tune heuristics. I'll add a composite dashboard panel but need events to be emitted from admission layer.

Ken Park: Proposal outline: 1) Lease slots remain for fast-path (N per device). 2) Coalesced admission uses soft tokens from a global budget. 3) Tokens carry a revocation TTL and a debt counter per-tenant. 4) When kv_evictions_per_minute crosses threshold, decay token budget and start marking oldest soft tokens preemptible. Sketch config:

```
admission:
  lease_slots_per_gpu: 4
  soft_token_budget: 250
  token:
    ttl_sec: 8
    per_tenant_soft_cap: 60
    decay_on_kv_evictions: 0.4
    min_budget: 20
```

Chen Li: We should tie decay_on_kv_evictions to a moving avg of eviction_rate so transient spikes don't kill bursts. And make ttl adaptive: longer ttl when batch_size is small.

Ravi Menon: For fairness, maintain a per-tenant score: tokens_granted - tokens_repaid (where repay happens as requests hit kv warm). If a tenant accumulates high debt, reduce their soft cap and shift them to a slower refill.

Priya Sharma: What about probing? A cheap randomized probe (1-in-100) to test a tenant's key warmness before granting a large coalesced token could prevent wasted bursts. If probe misses a lot, decline or give small-size grants.

Marta Gomez: For telemetry I can instrument: token_grants_by_tenant, token_debt_by_tenant, preemptible_eviction_events, probe_miss_rate. Also add a derived metric: eviction_sensitivity = corr(preemptible_evictions, kv_eviction_rate) over rolling window.

Avery Patel: Rollout safety: feature flag + shard canary. Also need an automated rollback if p99 rises > 10% or kv_hit_ratio drops > 5%.

Ken Park: I can build a micro-simulator that models tenants with different working sets and burstiness to validate parameters before runtime rollout. simulation-bot, can you spin that up?

simulation-bot: queued run sim-2026-03-23-01: 100 tenants, mixed hot/cold, baseline lease_slots=4, soft_budget=250, decay=0.4. Expected outputs: token_borrow_histogram, debt_distribution, p99_latency_heatmap.

Chen Li: Testing plan: unit tests for token lifecycle + an integration test in staging that replays cache-warm/cold traces. Also add a canary phase where decay_on_kv_evictions is initially 0.9 (conservative) for 48h then drop to target if stable.

Ravi Menon: Eviction policy detail: prefer to evict preemptible batches with largest expected remaining generation cost (est. tokens * avg_kv_miss_penalty) to reduce work wasted. We need a cheap estimator for remaining generation cost.

Priya Sharma: Edge-case: bots or internal tenants that do steady scans could game the system. Add an allowlist and also flag tenants with sustained probe_miss_rate > 0.7 for manual inspection.

Marta Gomez: I'll add alerts: probe_miss_rate > 0.3 for 5m, token_debt_tail > 90th percentile, and p99_increase > 8% during canary.

Avery Patel: Next actions: Ken builds the sim and a small prototype hook in admission; Chen writes probes + unit tests; Marta builds dashboards/alerts; Ravi writes SLO rollback thresholds; Priya drafts per-tenant debt policy and exception list. We'll gate behind feature-flag and run canary on shard-12 for a week.

Ken Park: I'll open an RFC follow-up with the simulator results and config matrix. We'll also include a simple bounded estimator for remaining generation cost.

Priya Sharma: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the working doc for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
